title: Runtime prioritizer and decision tracebook for policy evaluation
body:
Purpose and scope:

This note documents the runtime prioritizer component of the policy evaluation engine and the corresponding decision trace format we will emit from the serving runtime. It ties together constraints evaluation, scoring, cost-aware prioritization, and multi-region routing decisions under control-plane driven policy versions. The goal is a pragmatic, low-latency evaluation flow that: 1) produces a deterministic decision id and compact trace for observability; 2) supports partial evaluation and early-exit for common fast paths; 3) integrates cost signals for routing/variant selection; and 4) emits explainability logs at configurable verbosity without exposing PII.

Key concepts (quick glossary):
- Decision: a single routing/variant selection result for a request.
- Constraint: boolean checks (cap, whitelist, region-compat, model-compat) compiled from policy rules.
- Score: numeric ranking combining policy weight, cost-adjustment, and quality priors.
- Prioritizer: runtime stage that orders candidate variants by expected utility (score) and enforces capacity/latency SLO constraints.
- Trace: structured, append-only string payload (or proto) describing evaluation steps and outcomes.

High-level flow (runtime):
1) Ingest request metadata (customer, route, model hints, region preference, flags).
2) Resolve policy bundle from local control-plane cache (policy id + version).
3) Expand candidate set: apply static compatibility filters (architecture, quantization support, region availability).
4) Run constraint compiler: translate policy predicates into ordered constraint checks with short-circuiting.
5) Partial scoring pass: compute inexpensive heuristics (static cost, model-profile latency) and prune low-potential candidates.
6) Capacity-aware prioritization: consult local capacity map (per-variant token/s throughput) and apply soft caps.
7) Final scoring: evaluate quality priors and dynamic cost signals (predicted tokens, current price), produce final score for top-K candidates.
8) Decision commit: select winner, optional fallback list, generate decision trace, and route request.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Ordered constraints with early-exit: many constraints are cheap (region match, enterprise-level block) and drop most candidates quickly. We compile policy predicates into a canonical order: reject-short-circuit -> region/infra compat -> security/privacy checks -> cost thresholds -> A/B weights. This minimizes work in the common path.
- Two-pass scoring (partial then full): avoids heavy scoring work for candidates that will be pruned by cost or constraints. The partial pass uses cached model profiles + static pricing to compute a "baseline utility". Only top M candidates go through the final scoring that pulls live telemetry (queue lengths, pod latencies).
- Cost-aware score normalization: score = w_quality * quality_score - w_cost * normalized_expected_cost. Normalization uses a running median of expected per-token cost per model-variant at a granularity: (customer_tier, region, model_family). This helps compare candidates of different scales.
- Capacity soft-caps vs hard caps: to retain graceful degradation we prefer soft caps (score penalties once usage hits thresholds) with hard caps reserved only for explicit policy denies.

Decision trace format (requirements):
- Compact but queryable (must be indexable in Observability pipelines).
- Tamper-evident: include decision_id and short HMAC signed by instance key to verify integrity when ingested by control-plane UI.
- Configurable verbosity: three levels: MINIMAL, DIAGNOSTIC, FULL. MINIMAL is emitted by default in prod to limit bandwidth.
- Non-PII guaranteed: redaction rules applied before emission; any field marked sensitive by policy (e.g., prompt_text) is hashed or replaced with a token.

Proposed proto/string schema (human-readable):
- decision_id: <uuid>
- policy_version: <id@timestamp>
- request_meta: {route, customer_id_sha256, origin_region_hint}
- candidates_considered: N (integer)
- winner: {variant_id, score, reason_code}
- fallback_list: [variant_id:reason]
- constraints_evaluated: [list of constraint names with outcome times (ms) and pass/fail]
- scoring_breakdown: [for winner and top-3: {quality:float, cost:float, cap_penalty:float, final_score:float}]
- timings: {resolve_policy_ms, expand_candidates_ms, constraints_ms, scoring_ms, total_ms}
- instance_id: <host>
- signature: <hmac>

Note: the actual on-wire representation will be a compressed JSON line (newline-delimited) or a protobuf stored in S3/BigQuery depending on retention class. We will store MINIMAL traces in hot-store (30d) and FULL traces in cold archive (90d) with access logs.

Explainability log levels and sampling:
- MINIMAL: decision_id, winner.variant, policy_version, total_ms. Sampling: 1% per customer by default (configurable per-tier).
- DIAGNOSTIC: + constraints_evaluated (names + pass/fail), scoring_breakdown for winner. Sampling: 5% per customer for production, 100% for canaries.
- FULL: full scoring breakdown for top-K, redacted inputs, raw telemetry used for scoring. Only for internal debugging on opt-in or per-incident.

Privacy and security controls:
- Redaction policies are enforced at the trace emitter. We maintain a central redaction registry controlled in the control plane (fields flagged by name).
- Traces are signed with per-region instance keys; control plane has verification keys. Signatures detect replay/tamper.
- Access to FULL traces requires permissioned access via the console and IAM group (eng-platform-debug).

Multi-region considerations and control-plane interaction:
- Local policy cache: each region stores a compact policy bundle with TTL and ETag for rapid lookup. Control plane pushes new policy versions and can enforce an immediate invalidate via a push notification channel for high-severity fixes.
- Region-aware candidate expansion: we prefer local-region variants with score boost + lower cost estimate, but allow cross-region fallback when local capacity is insufficient or latency SLO acceptable per route.
- Cross-region fallbacks are annotated in traces (origin_region_hint -> chosen_region) to help analyze inter-region fallbacks frequency.
- Stale policy detection: a trace field flags if executed policy.version != control-plane current head for that policy id; used to drive rollout consistency audits.

Operational SLOs and observability metrics:
- Decision latency P50/P95/P99 targets (per-route).
- Constraint-eval time distribution; flag slow predicates ( > 2ms median) for review.
- Frequency of cross-region fallbacks and policy_staleness_count.
- Cost bias impact: measure rate of variant changes due to cost vs quality to ensure we do not over-optimize cost at expense of output quality.

Rollouts, canaries, and safety knobs:
- Policy version rollout via control plane supports staged traffic percentage. Prioritizer honors traffic-weights and records traffic-assignment in traces.
- Canary mode: set verbose trace sampling to 100% for selected customers and routes.
- Emergency rollback: control plane can flag a policy version as disabled; runtime does immediate local short-circuit and emits a special trace reason_code.

Future improvements roadmap (short list):
- Lightweight decision-graph cache: cache partial evaluation results keyed by request fingerprint for low-variance routes.
- ML-assisted scoring calibrator: use small bandit experiments to tune w_quality/w_cost per customer class.
- Structured trace ingestion with pre-aggregations for fast runbook queries (e.g., show recent fallbacks for customer X).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent multi-variant rollouts where we need to reserve capacity for both A and B simultaneously? (scheduling implications)
- Decide retention policy tiering defaults and cost allocations for trace storage.
- Finalize HMAC key rotation policy and integration with KMS/HSM.

Appendix (implementation notes):
- Keep constraint compiler side-effect free so it is easily testable and re-entrant.
- Instrument constraint functions with micro-timings (inlined) to attribute hotspots.
- Use a ring buffer of recent per-variant latencies as input to scoring to smooth spiky telemetry.

If this approach looks good I will draft an API sketch for the control plane endpoints (policy bundle delta, invalidate, sampling config) and a compact protobuf schema for the trace. Please call out any missing compliance requirements or telemetry quotas we should consider before locking the trace schema.
